get_label.description: Read the words of a drug's FDA label: the boxed warning, what it treats, how to take it, who must not take it, the warnings, the side effects, the interactions, the overdose advice and the rest, as plain text a summarizing or drafting step can use directly. Narrow it to the sections you want, or take the whole label. Ask by drug name or by Set ID. The boxed warning also comes back on its own, so a safety check is one step and one field.

search_labels.description: Find FDA drug labels by any combination of a drug name, the company on the label, a National Drug Code, an RxNorm code, an ingredient, a pharmacologic class, a controlled substance schedule, whether the medicine carries a boxed warning, how it was approved, and when the label was published. Every result comes back with the Set ID the other actions read, the publication date as a real date, and links to the label's page, its PDF and its archive. Searching by publication date is what a scheduled workflow watching for new or revised labels runs on.

description: Look up any FDA drug label from a workflow, straight from the National Library of Medicine. Search over 159,000 labels by drug name, manufacturer, National Drug Code, RxNorm code, ingredient, drug class, controlled substance schedule or publication date, then read the label itself as plain text: the boxed warning, what the medicine treats, how to take it, the warnings, the side effects and the interactions. Get a medicine's package codes, its strengths and pack sizes, its carton and tablet photographs, and every version of its label with the date each was published, so a scheduled workflow can notice the moment a label changes. Prescription, over-the-counter, animal and vaccine labels are all covered. Every action reads: nothing here changes anything. No account or API key required.
